problem_statement: There is no way to size a k_heap so that a requested allocation of N bytes reliably succeeds: a heap declared with N bytes has its usable capacity reduced by metadata (the heap header, bucket tables, the free list, the end marker and per-chunk headers), so small heaps can fail to allocate even a small fraction of their declared size. A helper should compute the minimum heap size required in order for an allocation of a given number of bytes to succeed, accounting for that metadata overhead, and the system heap should use it so that the configured memory pool can actually serve its advertised size.

problems.detail: The hidden test calls Z_HEAP_MIN_SIZE_FOR(base), but the problem statement only refers to an unnamed helper.
The statement does not specify that the helper must be a public preprocessor macro, available where heap-size macros such as Z_HEAP_MIN_SIZE are visible, and usable as a heap size argument.

problem_statement_fixed:
There is no way to size a k_heap so that a requested allocation of N bytes reliably succeeds: a heap declared with N bytes has its usable capacity reduced by metadata (the heap header, bucket tables, the free list, the end marker and per-chunk headers), so small heaps can fail to allocate even a small fraction of their declared size. A helper should compute the minimum heap size required in order for an allocation of a given number of bytes to succeed, accounting for that metadata overhead, and the system heap should use it so that the configured memory pool can actually serve its advertised size.

The helper should be a macro named Z_HEAP_MIN_SIZE_FOR, provided from include/zephyr/kernel.h, taking one argument that is the requested allocation size in bytes and expanding to a compile-time heap size in bytes. It should be usable in contexts that require a compile-time heap size, such as K_HEAP_DEFINE. When a heap is initialized with a size of Z_HEAP_MIN_SIZE_FOR(N), a single allocation of N bytes should succeed, and the returned size should not be less than N.
